newsitem.title: USA: Boise Cascade says paper business sluggish.
newsitem.headline: Boise Cascade says paper business sluggish.

text.p: Boise Cascade Corp said Monday it expects its paper business to remain sluggish until market conditions improve.

Boise Chairman and Chief Executive George Harad said in a statement that the company also expects its office products distribution business to show higher operating income, and the building products segment is likely to weaken seasonally in the fourth quarter.

"Average prices for all grades of paper produced by Boise Cascade were lower in the third quarter of 1996 than in the prior periods, and several of the company's pulp and paper mills experienced unanticipated production outages," the company said in its earnings statement.

On an operating basis, the company said its paper business generated a profit of $10.1 million in the third quarter versus operating income of $164 million one year ago and an operating loss of $15.2 million in the second quarter.
Boise Cascade Corp said its third quarter results improved from the previous quarter due to solid demand for paper, despite experiencing work outages at some mills and despite a drop in paper prices.
The company said paper sales volume totaled 729,000 short tons in the third quarter, up from 656,000 tons in the second quarter.

Earlier, the company reported a net loss of $0.24 a share in the third quarter, well off its $1.83 per share profit one year ago. But the results beat analysts's expectations of a loss of $0.28 a share, according to First Call.

The company's office products unit rebounded from a slow start early in the period, reporting operating income of $22.0 million in the third quarter compared with operating income of $21.2 million in the prior year's third quarter, the company said.

However, operating income dipped in the third quarter from the second quarter -- when the company recorded $24.9 million in operating income -- primarily because of continued competitive pressures on gross margins, it said.
Boise shares were up 1/4 at 33-1/4 by mid-morning.
